description:
Get the encryption keypair for an approval channel. With `hitl:read` it returns the public key, encrypted private key, KDF salt, and key ID (kid). A key holding `confirmations:create` without `hitl:read` receives only `public_key` and `kid` — what a confirmation message is sealed to, never the private-key material.

ACCESS: needs a Proof account. Authenticate this client (Claude Code: /mcp → Authenticate), then call this tool again. start_login does NOT open this tool.
name: get_approval_channel_keys

outputSchema.description: A HITL config's keypair. A caller with `hitl:read` (or a dashboard session) gets every field; a key holding `confirmations:create` without `hitl:read` gets `public_key` and `kid` only.

backup_wrapped_dek.description: The same data key wrapped under the recovery key; null until recovery is set up

encrypted_private_key.description: The private key as stored, wrapped client-side. Absent for a key holding `confirmations:create` without `hitl:read`.

kdf_salt.description: The salt the wrapping key is derived with. Absent for a key holding `confirmations:create` without `hitl:read`.

kid.description: The key id: lowercase hex SHA-256 of the public key's SPKI DER

public_key.description: The RSA public key (SPKI PEM) messages are sealed to. Null means the stored key material could not be read: a degraded state to report, not "no key yet" (a config with no keypair answers 404 `no_keypair`).

wrapped_dek.description: The per-config data key wrapped under the master key; null for a keypair stored before it existed. Absent for a requester key, as are the five fields below.
